comments.content: Behavior change: the original called `dict.Get("statusCode", &status_code)` which, if the JS `statusCode` value is present but of a non-int type, would leave `status_code` at its initialized value `net::HTTP_OK` (Get returns false, but status_code was pre-set). With `ValueOrDefault`, the internal `value` starts at `T{}` (0), and if `Get` fails it returns `default_value` (net::HTTP_OK). This is functionally equivalent here. No issue — but note the `static_cast<int>` is required since `net::HTTP_OK` is an enum; template arg deduction now yields `T=int`, so this is correct.

`item.slider.minValue`/`maxValue`/`doubleValue` are `double` (CGFloat). Previously the code read into `int` locals then assigned. `ValueOrDefault("value", 50)` deduces `T=int`, so a JS float value (e.g. 50.5) would now fail to convert into an `int` and fall back to the default, silently truncating/discarding fractional slider values. If floats were previously accepted (unlikely given the old int locals), behavior is unchanged; but if the API intends to accept fractional values consider using a double default (e.g. `50.0`). Please verify the documented type for slider min/max/value.
